blockers.quote: Misconception first: you believed time and money are separate currencies.
blockers.why: story #7: The opening rule already proves that time and money are exchangeable, so this belief is broken before you act on it rather than by the midpoint fact.
blockers.fix: Replace with: “You believe only the app sells time, so you tap to escape years of work and debt. Then the surgery cost becomes internship hours on screen; those hours peel off your figure as Papa watches, proving ordinary money was already buying your life.”

blockers.quote: The wordless peak: each work-hour card folds into a year and drops off your figure.
blockers.why: story #6: Reaching Papa’s age implies many additional taps, but those uses have neither a stated expectation nor a different result.
blockers.fix: At about 78%, have Papa slide the phone away: his second operation, or his wish that you stop. You take it back and tap. You expect each cleared charge to be the last; each receipt reveals the next charge. Repeat that gap through the montage until your hand matches his, then land the existing reversal.

suggestions.quote: One tap: you age one year in a second and the money arrives
suggestions.fix: Define the payout: “The app pays the exact bill shown on screen—one bill, one year.” Then make every later payment a distinct tap.

suggestions.quote: One grey eyebrow hair, and the bill is paid.
suggestions.fix: Add immediately: “Not a filter. Your whole body is one year older.” Show the hand and posture changing with the eyebrow.

suggestions.quote: You pay your mother's phone bill, the twice-a-day calls, and you don't tell her.
suggestions.fix: Cut this dangling branch and spend the time on Papa’s bus-pass tease; Mum never affects the later choice or turn.

suggestions.quote: The bill he hid under his pillow, the one he says is nothing
suggestions.fix: Move this reveal after seven seconds. Keep the opening seven seconds to the phone, sleeping Papa, hovering hand, and spoken title question.

suggestions.quote: ## Beat outline (runtime shares; length estimated 7 to 8 minutes, the script decides)
suggestions.fix: The estimate passes length. If the script crosses 8:00, the felt reason to stay is whether you choose Papa’s second operation or the years you could still share with him; leave immediately after the bus-pass image.

keep.quote: One year from me buys him ten. Good deal.
you did not buy ten years with him; you bought ten years he may have without you.
He's teasing you about the bus pass again. You let him.
